content.value_statement: Plans often fail when tasks lack owners, dependencies, or clear starting conditions. This skill turns accepted Paperclip plans into a verified task graph that supports focused and parallel execution.
actual_capabilities: Break an accepted plan into concrete Paperclip issues.
Match each task to an agent specialty and identify ownership gaps.
Define blockers with blockedByIssueIds instead of parent-child ordering.
Identify independent tasks that can begin in parallel.
Create a compact task matrix with owners, statuses, and blockers.
Verify the created issue graph before closing the planning issue.
limitations: It does not create a plan format or replace planning judgment.
It does not install, configure, or operate Paperclip.
It requires an accepted plan and current information about available agents.
It cannot resolve missing skills, approvals, hires, or external dependencies.

use_cases.title: Prepare an engineering release
use_cases.description: Turn a release plan into owned implementation, testing, documentation, and rollout tasks with explicit blockers.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a marketing launch
use_cases.description: Separate research, creative, approval, channel setup, and reporting work so independent teams can start together.

use_cases.title: Organize an operations initiative
use_cases.description: Convert an approved process change into traceable tasks, dependencies, and completion checks.

prompt_templates.title: Start with a simple breakdown
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this accepted plan into Paperclip tasks. For each task, provide an owner, initial status, blockers, and a reason if it can start now: [paste plan].

prompt_templates.title: Assign work by specialty
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this plan and these agent specialties, create a task matrix. Assign each task to the best-suited agent and identify any capability gaps: Plan: [paste plan]. Agents: [paste agents].

prompt_templates.title: Build a dependency graph
prompt_templates.prompt: Translate this approved plan into Paperclip issues. Use blockedByIssueIds for every hard dependency. Do not use parent-child nesting or prose as execution blocking: [paste plan].

prompt_templates.title: Verify completed task creation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Paperclip task list against the source plan. Find missing deliverables, incorrect blockers, unclear owners, and tasks that should start in parallel: Plan: [paste plan]. Tasks: [paste tasks].

output_examples.input: A plan requires customer research before finalizing messaging and publishing a launch page.
output: Research customer needs — Owner: Research agent — Status: open — Can start now: required input is available.
Define messaging — Owner: Marketing agent — Status: blocked — Blocker: customer research.
Publish launch page — Owner: Web agent — Status: blocked — Blocker: approved messaging.

output_examples.input: A plan contains independent security review and documentation work after implementation.
output_examples.output: The implementation task is the shared blocker. Security review and documentation become separate tasks that can run in parallel after implementation is done.

best_practices: Make every concrete deliverable a separate issue with one deliberate owner.
Use blockedByIssueIds for hard dependencies and state why unblocked work can start.
Re-fetch and verify the issue graph before closing the source planning issue.
anti_patterns: Do not treat parent-child nesting or task order as an execution blocker.
Do not assign work by default to the planner when another specialty fits better.
Do not hide missing skills, approvals, or external inputs inside vague tasks.

faq.question: Does this skill provide a plan template?
faq.answer: No. It works with any accepted plan format and focuses on converting that plan into executable tasks.

faq.question: How should I represent a blocker?
faq.answer: Add the prerequisite issue IDs to blockedByIssueIds on the dependent task.

faq.question: Can the same agent own parallel tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. Independent tasks can run in parallel when the agent and environment support concurrent work.

faq.question: Should parent-child issues block execution?
faq.answer: No. Use parent-child relationships for traceability only, and use explicit blocker fields for execution dependencies.

faq.question: What happens when no agent has the needed specialty?
faq.answer: Record the gap clearly. It may require a hire, tool, external dependency, or board decision.

faq.question: When should I close the planning issue?
faq.answer: Close it only after verifying that created tasks have correct owners, blockers, and start conditions.
